done_when: Close no longer runs the full test command on the laptop when the pull request's CI runs it: it runs fast_test when set, otherwise only the test files the change touched and the tests named after its changed source files; CI still runs the full suite and a red CI sends the item back. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body:
Close reports no matching tests when a change touches `__tests__/cart.js`, and it misses that file when `cart.js` changes.
Raise: Not done — The filename filter checks only the basename for `.test`, `.spec`, and similar patterns. [Jest's default test discovery](https://jestjs.io/docs/30.0/configuration) also includes ordinary JavaScript and TypeScript files under `__tests__`. The named Jest proofs use only `.test` and `.spec` files, so they do not cover this normal layout.
findings.title: Not done: Close skips Jest's default __tests__ files

findings.body:
Changing a helper-only `helpers_test.go` file produces no Go command, so Close succeeds without even compiling the changed test package.
Raise: Functional — The file is selected, but `names` is empty and the `if names` guard drops the package. [Go compiles every active `_test.go` file](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Test_packages), including helper files without test functions. The Go proof changes files containing test functions; its shared helper file stays unchanged.
findings.title: Not done: Go test helper edits run no local package check

findings.body:
A valid command such as `uv sync && uv run pytest tests` fails in setup during Close because selected test filenames are appended to `uv sync`.
Raise: Functional — `src/forge/quicktest.py:51–57` classifies `uv sync` as an unrecognized part, and this fallback appends the selected filenames to it. The shipped guide at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:986` promises to keep setup arguments. The command proofs cover direct pytest and npm setup, but not a Python setup step.
findings.title: Close passes test filenames to Python setup commands

why: Each round runs the same tests twice, on the laptop and in CI, which is most of a round's time
